title: When Helpful Advice Starts Sounding Like Criticism
summary: Use NEW → NECESSARY → THEIRS to keep useful parental guidance, match authority to the real stake, and return age-appropriate ownership to your teenager.
seo_title: When Teen Advice Sounds Like Criticism
seo_description: Why does your teenager reject helpful advice? Audit what is new, what is necessary, and what decision or action can remain theirs.
release_move: Use NEW → NECESSARY → THEIRS to add only needed information, preserve safety and real boundaries, and return the remaining age-appropriate decision, action, or learning consequence to the teenager.

core_belief_shift.from: If my teenager rejects correct advice, I need to explain the lesson more clearly or firmly until they accept it.
core_belief_shift.to: Correct guidance is more useful when I add what is genuinely new, match my authority to the actual stake, and leave my teenager an age-appropriate part to own.

book_relevance.reason: The article completes a parent reflection and ownership-transfer job; a Playbook bridge would add product pressure without serving the reader's immediate need.
